endorsements.quote: Alignment is implemented through procurement and governance requirements that mandate a declared clinical purpose mapped to the P3H pathway, named accountable clinical and operational owners, and documented participatory design.

Alignment involves participatory co-design with clinicians and communities to ensure tools reflect contextual realities, such as using chatbots in community health clinics to improve medication adherence among low-literacy populations.
Equity mandates stratified evaluation and mitigation plans with time-bound improvement targets to ensure that gains in efficiency or average performance do not widen disparities.

unlisted_practices: Set a minimum whole-person data standard and require interoperable, structured exchange of clinical, behavioral, omics, and contextual data through procurement for AI-enabled care pathways.
Shift payment systems from volume-based incentives toward value-based structures that reward continuity, prevention, and coordination.
Embed data science, genomics, behavioral science, and digital ethics, AI fluency, and systems thinking into undergraduate and postgraduate medical training.
Tie AI reporting and payment to patient-reported outcomes, functional status, preventable utilization, and total cost rather than model discrimination alone.
Use privacy-preserving architectures such as federated learning when integrating whole-person data across institutions.
Implement pathway-level workflow standards including defined handoffs, escalation processes, human override, audit trails, and safety monitoring.

screen.reason: The paper is a conceptual blueprint and policy framework (the AI-WHOLE framework) proposing governance principles and operational integration of AI for whole-person care.
